positioning: The Gray Ghost with eyes like amber glass.
story: A Weimaraner moves like smoke. Silver coat, amber eyes, and no sound at all. It does not walk up to you. It appears.

The breed began in Weimar, Germany, in the early 1800s. Grand Duke Karl August and his court wanted a fast, fearless hunter for deer, boar, and bear. Nobles guarded the breed closely and rarely sold a dog.
Later the dogs turned to birds, and the Weimaraner became a versatile gun dog. It points, tracks, and retrieves. The AKC recognized the breed in 1943.
Then it became a star. Photographer William Wegman posed his Weimaraners in costume for decades and made them art-world royalty. President Eisenhower kept one named Heidi at the White House.
At home, a Weimaraner is a shadow with opinions. It follows you from room to room. It loves its people so much that being alone feels like a punishment. It needs miles of running every day.
Give it a lake, a long trail, and a job, and you will have a steady ghost at your heel for life.
rank_cap: The Gray Ghost of German nobility (AKC)
fblocks: Named for Weimar, the German city of the grand duke’s court. The Gray Ghost comes from the coat and the silent stride.
Heidi, who lived in the Eisenhower White House. Man Ray and Fay Ray, stars of William Wegman’s photographs.
Needs hard exercise and constant company. Lonely Weimaraners turn destructive. The deep chest raises the risk of bloat.
A short, sleek coat in silver, mouse, or blue-gray. Eyes run amber, gray, or blue-gray.
Fifty-five to ninety pounds. Bred in Germany in the early 1800s. Recognized by the AKC in 1943.
days: Ash lies with his chin on the dock plank. The lake can wait. So can he.
The Weimaraner started in Weimar, Germany, for the grand duke’s hunts.
Ghost points on the dune crest. Paw up, tail straight, the whole sky holding still.
Bandanas on, ears back, and the pontoon in no hurry. A fine Wednesday.
A bobber floats. A Weimaraner watches. Patience looks good in silver.
Weimaraner puppies are born with faint tiger stripes. They fade in days.
Puppies asleep in an overturned kayak. Sandy paws, pale blue eyes, no plans.
last_walk:
The pier lights flick on, and the lake turns to pewter.
Ghost walks beside old Ash toward the little lighthouse. The young dog slows to the old dog’s pace. Silver coats, silver water. A Weimaraner is a ghost only to strangers. To its people it is the warmest thing on the pier.
